newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-German building union, employers avert strike.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German building union, employers avert strike.

text.p: Germany's troubled construction industry averted the threat of its first big strike since 1950 on Friday when the IG Bau union and building employers agreed a compromise wage deal.
The agreement came just five days before a deadline after which the union could have balloted members for strike action which would have threatened to plunge the sector even deeper into recession.
The new deal offers better sick pay arrangements than an earlier proposal which the union's wages commission had rejected on Monday.
But employers still expect a reduction in labour costs via a below-inflation pay rise and falls in sick pay and holiday bonus entitlements.

The pay rise of 1.3 percent -- less than the rate of inflation -- was agreed after arbitration talks last week brokered by Heiner Geissler, a senior politician from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats.
"The agreement makes an important contribution towards safeguarding jobs," German construction minister Klaus Toepfer said.

The deal covers 1.3 million workers in west Germany, of whom about 400,000 are unemployed. The two sides failed to agree on pay for 380,000 construction workers in east Germany and said they would resume talks at a later date.
Friday's deal has already been ratified by the industry's two employer federations as well as by the union's wages commission, which is made up of regional representatives.
Sick pay will be cut by 20 percent only for the first three days of sickness instead of for the first three weeks, as proposed last week.
That means that after the first three day of illness, sick pay will return to 100 percent of normal wages.
The three-week reduction in sick pay had been the main bone of contention and the reason why the original deal had been rejected.
"The union got the best it could out of the talks," IG Bau chairman Klaus Wiesehuegel told a news conference.
The building employers' concession on sick pay was made in return for a reduction in holiday bonuses to 25 percent of monthly pay from 30 percent.
Christmas bonuses will be cut to 77 percent of a month's pay and will also be reduced in the event of sickness.

The German building industry, seen as having the highest costs in the world, is suffering from a surplus of capacity now that the east German building boom which followed unification in 1990 has fizzled out.
